title: {{NAME}} and the Midnight Parliament
moral: True councils make space for all voices, even the quietest.
character_anchor: Bright children's book cartoon illustration, bold outlines, vivid flat colours. {{NAME}}, a young boy with brown hair and blue eyes, wearing a silver-green tunic, dark green trousers, and boots with leaf engravings — same child, same face, same exact outfit in every image.

pages.content:
The Midnight Parliament was the oldest institution in the kingdom, and almost nobody knew it existed.

It met once a month, at the full moon, in the palace's oldest courtyard.

Members: Princess Rowan (current chair), the unicorn Meridian (oldest living member), and representatives of every animal species in the kingdom.

{{NAME}} had been appointed minutes secretary because of his handwriting, which was exceptionally clear, and because he was the only page who didn't make the badger delegate nervous.

pages.content:
The parliament dealt with matters that concerned the whole kingdom: seasonal migrations that crossed human roads, water rights that affected fish populations upstream of farming settlements, forest edge agreements between logging and nesting seasons.

Most humans didn't know these agreements existed.

Most of what kept the kingdom in balance was negotiated in this courtyard by moonlight.

{{NAME}} wrote very fast and very small and understood, over the first three months, that he was writing the most important documents in the kingdom.

pages.content:
His most important contribution came in month four.

A dispute between the river otter delegation and the farming community downstream had been stalled for eight months because neither side was using the same definition of water rights.

{{NAME}} had been taking minutes for both. He noticed the misalignment.

In a pause, he raised his hand and read out the two different definitions side by side.

Silence.

Then the otter delegate said: "Oh. We have been arguing about different things."

"Yes," said {{NAME}}, as gently as possible.

pages.content:
The resolution took twenty minutes once everyone understood what they were actually discussing.

Meridian the unicorn walked to {{NAME}} afterward and touched her horn briefly to his notepad.

"The minutes secretary who clarifies," she said.

"I just read back what was said," said {{NAME}}.

"In four months, no one has done that before you," she said.

Princess Rowan, signing the resolution: "He'll be permanent secretary."

{{NAME}} had not applied for this but found he was not opposed.

pages.content:
He walked home as the moon set, his minutes book under his arm.

Thirty-seven species represented. One hundred and twelve agenda items in four months. Forty-eight resolutions.

None of it visible during the day. The kingdom in balance because of meetings nobody knew about.

{{NAME}} thought: this is what government looks like when it works.

In bed, he fell asleep with his pen still in his hand, and in his dreams he was still writing, fast and clear, keeping the perfect record of everything the kingdom said to itself in the dark.
